summary: An accessor (getter) method returns a private field's value, and a mutator (setter) method changes it. A mutator can check a new value before it saves it.
notes: #gpa is a private field. Inside the class you write this.#gpa, with the # every time.
setGpa only saves newGpa when it is between 0.0 and 4.0.
maya.getGpa() needs parentheses to call the method. Mutators like setGpa return nothing, so they give back undefined.
pitfall: Writing maya.#gpa outside the class causes SyntaxError: Private field '#gpa' must be declared in an enclosing class, before any line runs. Use maya.getGpa() instead.
contrast: A # field is blocked outside the class like Java's private, not just marked by convention like Python's underscore. As in both, mutators usually return nothing, which in JavaScript means undefined.
